The sun hung low, casting a golden glow over the garden, where wildflowers sprawled chaotically, their vibrant colors fighting for attention amidst the stubborn weeds. Mara knelt in the cool earth, her fingers digging into the soil, feeling the dampness seep into her skin like a soothing balm. The rich scent of life filled the air, mingling with the faint tang of rust from the wrought-iron gate that creaked softly in the gentle breeze. She paused, brushing a damp lock of hair away from her forehead, the moisture clinging stubbornly to her skin.

“Are you going to bury yourself in there, or do you plan to actually plant something?” The teasing voice cut through the quiet, playful yet tinged with genuine curiosity.

Mara looked up to see Tom leaning against the gatepost, arms crossed over his chest, the late afternoon sun catching the tousled strands of his hair, giving him an almost ethereal glow. His presence felt familiar and grounding, as if he was a part of this garden just as much as the tangled vines climbing the old stone walls. She fought the flutter of annoyance that threatened to rise at his lighthearted jab, allowing herself only a half-smile.

“Just trying to coax the life back into it,” she replied, her voice softer than she intended, the warmth of the moment wrapping around her like a soft shawl. “These flowers remind you of what was once here.”

Tom stepped closer, the gravel crunching beneath his boots, the sound harmonizing with the whispering leaves. He peered over her shoulder, taking in the riot of petals and thorns that formed a chaotic tapestry. “Life has a funny way of coming back, doesn’t it?” he mused, his gaze drifting thoughtfully. “Just like us, I guess.”
